plan_summary.objective: Refine the existing subagent permission/tooling proposal into an executable direction for goals 1-3 only: fewer meaningless authorization interruptions, preserved least privilege, and enforceable tool-preference rules with no bash exploration fallback.
plan_summary.recommended_approach: Proceed with the proposal after four refinements: explicitly split goals 1-3 from later gate/legacy work, formalize `edit: allow` for non-implementation agents as artifact-only via prompt/test constraints, rewrite Tool Usage Policy into MUST-first rules with explicit exceptions/remediation and no bash fallback, and normalize remaining git permissions as observational only rather than an exploration path.
major_implementation_steps: Trim or clearly defer sections related to gate strengthening and legacy cleanup so this change stays bounded to goals 1-3.
Update the permission matrix so non-implementation agents use `edit: allow` with explicit artifact-only write boundaries and no general repo editing authority.
Add a unified Tool Usage Policy with executable MUST-first rules for memory/codegraph, Glob/Grep/Read, context7, tavily, headroom, and mandatory skill invocation.

Add explicit exception/remediation language so doc-only work and known-file artifact work do not force unnecessary tool use, and unavailable/insufficient preferred tools produce blockers instead of bash degradation.
Define role-specific read-only git allowances strictly as observational workflow/repository inspection, not as codebase exploration fallback.
Back the prompt/frontmatter changes with contract tests and scenario-level review criteria.
focused_verification_strategy: Assert frontmatter permissions and allowed observational git patterns per agent in `tests/test_wrapper_contracts.py`.
Assert prompt language for artifact-only write boundaries, MUST-first tool rules, explicit no-bash-degradation semantics, and remediation/blocker behavior.
Assert destructive git/shell commands remain blocked.
Review typical agent paths to confirm plan/test/review/finish can write required artifacts without meaningless auth interruptions and without reverting to bash exploration.

review_summary.conclusion: The design is now specific enough to proceed without another approval turn.
strengths: Correctly identifies the contract-vs-permission mismatch for artifact-writing agents.
Uses the accepted least-privilege compromise: `edit: allow` plus prompt/test constraints instead of broader runtime changes.
Upgrades tooling policy from soft recommendations to enforceable behavior.
Removes bash exploration fallback entirely, which keeps policy aligned with high-level tools rather than shell habits.
recommended_design_refinements: State near the top that this iteration implements only goals 1-3.
Explicitly define non-implementation-agent write authority as workflow-artifact-only despite `edit: allow`.
Rewrite Tool Usage Policy as decision rules with MUST/PREFER/ONLY-WHEN plus explicit exception and remediation behavior.
Define unavailable or insufficient preferred tools as blocker/remediation cases rather than justification for bash fallback.
Keep per-role git allowances specific and observational only.
non_blocking_risks: Prompt-only boundaries can drift if prompt-contract tests are weak.
No-bash-degradation may expose more blockers when high-level tools are unavailable or misconfigured.
Too many MUST rules can bloat prompts unless exception language is concise and reused.
assumptions: Canonical edits will be made in `agents/*.md` and then distributed to CLI-specific copies.
Static prompt/frontmatter contract tests are the primary enforcement mechanism for this iteration.
Gate-quality strengthening and legacy cleanup remain out of scope for this execution cycle.
